## TL;DR
Human-assigned tasks now get a `## Step-by-step guide` requirement: PM and engineer prompts demand it, `repoos new`/`update`/the API warn when it is missing, the scaffold includes the heading, and `repoos update --section` can edit it alone. This round closes the last review class (markdown fences) everywhere it appears.

## Work and rationale
- `src/core/markdown-fence.ts`: new `markdownFenceOpen` (CommonMark: a backtick fence's info string cannot contain a backtick, so `` ```inline``` text `` is inline code) and `markdownFenceMask` (per-line "inside or on a fence").
- `src/core/task.ts`: `sectionStart` now ignores a heading shown inside a fenced sample, so `extractSection`, `replaceSection` and `removeSection` act on the real section; `nextSection` and `collectActivityEntries` already tracked fences (previous round) and use the shared opener.
- `src/core/task-underspecified.ts`: `bundleSpecSections` skips fenced `## ` lines; guide extraction uses the shared opener. `src/core/task-summary.ts` uses the shared opener too.
- Tests in `src/core/task-section-fence.test.ts`: fenced `## ` line, fenced sample holding the heading itself ahead of the real guide, closing fence with an info string, and the inline-backticks case.

## Approaches tried
One shared mask helper instead of another per-function scanner, since each review pass found the next copy of the same class.

## Challenges and blockers
Five unrelated `src/core` tests fail under bare vitest in this worktree (attachment-migration, canary, git-maintenance-lsof, task-dependencies); they are environment-sensitive and untouched by this diff.

## Key learnings
Every markdown scan over task bodies (section start, section end, activity, bundles, summary) must share one fence tracker.
